sanskrit: namaḥ piśaṅgabāhvai sindhau jātāyā ugrāyai | yo asyai nama it karad aped asya gṛhād ayat ||
english: Homage to the tawny-armed one, the fierce one born in the Sindhu — whoever pays homage to her, he departs away from this man's house.

sanskrit: apehi no gṛhebhyo apehi vatsatantyāḥ | ātmānam atra rotsyasy ava roha mahānasāt ||
english: Depart from our houses, depart from the calf-rope! You will entangle yourself right here — come down from the kitchen.

sanskrit: hā amba suhūtale atho hai sāmanantame | putro yas te pṛśnibāhus tam u tvaṃ sāmanaṃ kṛdhi | atho duhitaraṃ naptrīm atho tvaṃ sāmanā bhava ||
english: Hā, O mother, O Suhūtalā! And also, O Sāmanantamā! Your son who is spotted-armed — make him your sāman; and also your daughter, your granddaughter — and you yourself become reconciled.

sanskrit: bhūtapatir nir ajatv indraś cetaḥ sadānvāḥ | gṛhasya budhna āsīnās tā vajreṇādhi tiṣṭhatu ||
english: Let Bhūtapati drive them out, let Indra drive out the mind-afflicting Sadānvās! May he who is seated at the foundation of the house stand over them with his thunderbolt.

sanskrit: apetetaḥ sadānvā ahiṃsantīr imaṃ gṛham | dhenur vātra ya sthāsyaty anaḍvān verayā saha ||
english: Depart hence, O Sadānvās, not harming this house! Let the milch-cow who stands here remain, along with the draft-ox and the heifer.

sanskrit: yā sahamānā carasi sāsahāna iva rṣabhaḥ | sadānvāghnīṃ tvā vayaṃ jaitrāyācchā vadāmasi ||
english: You who roam as one who overpowers, like a bull that has prevailed — we address you as the Sadānvā-slayer, for the purpose of victory.

sanskrit: sahasva no abhimātiṃ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | sahasva sarvā rakṣāṃsi sahamānāsy oṣadhe ||
english: Overpower our malevolent foe, overpower the one arrayed in battle against us! Overpower all the rākṣasas — you are the overpowering one, O plant!

sanskrit: tvaṃ vyāghrān sahase tvaṃ siṃhām̐ ubhayādataḥ | makṣāś cit kṛṇvānā madhu tvaṃ sahasa oṣadhe ||
english: You overpower tigers, you overpower lions with teeth on both jaws; even bees that make honey — you overpower them, O plant!

sanskrit: iyaṃ pitre rāṣṭry ety agre prathamāya januṣe bhūmaniṣṭhāḥ | tasmā etaṃ surucaṃ hvāram ahyaṃ gharmaṃ śrīṇanti prathamasya dhāsyoḥ ||
english: This sovereign lady goes forward to the Father, to the first-born, to those who stand firm on the earth. For him they prepare this radiant, serpent-like gharma-vessel of the first nourishing draught.

sanskrit: brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ purastād vi sīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ | sa budhnyā upamā asya viṣṭhāḥ sataś ca yonim asataś ca vi vaḥ ||
english: Brahman, born first in the east, the seer Vena illumined it beyond the limits with brilliant light. Its supreme stations are those of the foundation — it opened wide the womb of what exists and of what does not exist.

sanskrit: pra yo jajñe vidvām̐ asya bandhuṃ viśvāni devo janimā vivakti | brahma brahmaṇa uj jabhāra madhyān nīcād uccā svadhā abhi pra tasthau ||
english: He who was born knowing the kinship of this — the god speaks forth all births; Brahman seized Brahman up from the midst, rising from low to high, and self-power stood forth.

sanskrit: mahān mahī askabhāyad vi jāto dyāṃ dvitaḥ pārthivaṃ ca rajaḥ | sa budhnād āṣṭra januṣābhy agraṃ bṛhaspatir devatā tasya samrāṭ ||
english: The great one propped apart the vast realm when born; a second time, heaven and the earthly atmosphere. Arising from the foundation by birth to the foremost position — Bṛhaspati is his deity, the universal sovereign.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ tad asya gavyaṃ hinoti maho devasya pūrvasya mahi | eṣa jajñe bahubhiḥ sākam itthā pūrvād ardhād avithuraś ca san nu ||
english: Now that cow-domain drives forward the greatness of this great, primal deity. He was born thus, together with the many, and indeed he shall be unwavering from the former half.

sanskrit: sa hi divaḥ sa pṛthivyā ṛteṣṭhā mahi kṣāman rajasī vi ṣkabhāyati | ahar yac chukraṃ jyotiṣo janiṣṭa- -adhā dyumanto vi vasantv ariprāḥ ||
english: For he, standing by cosmic order in heaven and on earth, props apart the great atmospheric spaces, the two realms. When the radiant day was born from the light, may the luminous, unstained ones shine forth.

sanskrit: evātharvā pitaraṃ viśvadevaṃ bṛhaspatir namasāvocad accha | tvaṃ viśvasya janitā dhāsy agre kavir devān na dabhāya svadhāvaḥ ||
english: Thus Atharva-Bṛhaspati addressed the all-divine Father with homage: "You are the begettor of the universe, you sustain first — the wise poet, self-powerful, not betraying the gods."

sanskrit: mūrdhnā yo agram abhyarty ojasā bṛhaspatim ā vivāsanti devāḥ | bhinad valaṃ vi mṛdho dardarīti kanikradad gāḥ svar apo jigāya ||
english: He who approaches the foremost with his head, with might — the gods worship Bṛhaspati: he split Vala apart, he shatters foes with a crash, bellowing he conquered the cows, the sun, and the waters.

sanskrit: ud apaptad asau sūryaḥ purudṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā | udāyan raśmibhir hantu- -udāyann arasām̐ akaḥ ||
english: That sun has flown up, the widely-seen, the slayer of the unseen. Rising, may he smite with his rays — rising he rendered them devoid of potency.

sanskrit: ny amrucad asau sūryo viśvadṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā | nimrocan raśmibhir hantu nimrocann arasām̐ akaḥ ||
english: That sun has set, the universally-seen, the slayer of the unseen. Setting, may he smite with his rays — setting he rendered them devoid of potency.

sanskrit: ye ca dṛṣṭā ye cādṛṣṭā ubhayehāviṣyavaḥ | teṣāṃ vo agrabhaṃ nāma sarve sākaṃ ni jasyata ||
english: Both those that are seen and those that are unseen — those active in both modes here — I have seized their name; let them all perish together.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭahananī vīrud amitaujā viṣāsahi | cukākaṇi tvaṃ jajñiṣe sādṛṣṭāñ jātaśo jahi ||
english: O herb, slayer of the unseen, of unmeasured power, victorious over poison — O Cukākaṇi, you were born to slay the seen ones; slay them by species.

sanskrit: jahi jyeṣṭham adṛṣṭānāṃ sarpāṇāṃ moghacāriṇām | krimīṇāṃ sarvā jātāni ?pauñjaṣṭa iva yavaṃ mṛṇa ||
english: Slay the chief of the unseen ones, of the serpents that roam in vain! Crush all species of worms as a thresher crushes barley.

sanskrit: yaś ca todo yaś ca sarpa ekādaśaś ca yo vṛṣā | cukākaṇi tvaṃ tān vṛśca vṛkṣaṃ paraśumān iva ||
english: Both the stinger and the creeper, and that one who is the eleventh male — O Cukākaṇi, cut them all down as a man with an axe cuts a tree.

sanskrit: saṃ vṛścaināṃś cukākaṇi vṛkṣaṃ paraśumān iva | krimīṇāṃ sarvā jātāni saṃ dahāgnir ivolapam ||
english: Cut them down together, O Cukākaṇi, as a man with an axe cuts a tree! Burn all species of worms together as fire burns dry grass.

sanskrit: methiṣṭhā agnir aghalas tviṣīmān krimīṇāṃ jātāni pra dunotu sarvā | bṛhaspater medine jātavedā adṛṣṭān hantu dṛṣadeva māṣān ||
english: Agni, standing at the post, blazing, full of splendor — let him torment all species of worms! O Jātavedas, allied with Bṛhaspati, smite the unseen ones as a millstone smites black beans.
